hypotheses.title: Signed edge-pair cancellation as a non-fault-body veto
hypotheses.potential_label: Highest qualitative potential in this revised shortlist; no measured improvement
layers: depth_to_base_surf (owner-mirror band 15; conductive-base depth proxy only)
hypotheses.signature: Along gravity-edge normals, sample signed cross-normal gradient profiles at fixed 200, 400 and 800 m smoothing scales. Distinguish a persistent monotonic step from a balanced pair of opposite-polarity lobes returning to background; penalize the latter as a finite-width body hypothesis. Require consistency along strike, not just a high local gradient.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried density step can persist under basin fill without a mapped surface trace. This hypothesis tries to reject finite-width magnetic bodies rather than reward proximity to the public catalogue. Some real fault zones also produce paired lobes, so the veto must earn its value on buffered hide-and-recover folds.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The local MSPTCD implementation uses unsigned shifted gradient amplitudes and local orientation products, not signed profile return-to-background or paired-lobe cancellation. This is a proposed discriminant, not the already-tested depth-shifted-concordance H1. Prior fleet-wide use cannot be excluded.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: A one-sided unfaulted intrusive or lithologic contact can still resemble a structural step; a real horst or narrow fault-bounded block can resemble a finite-width body and be incorrectly vetoed.

hypotheses.title: Radiometric-quiet magnetic-edge transfer under conductive cover
hypotheses.potential_label: Moderate qualitative potential; targets a mapping-bias regime rather than more dots
layers: tc (owner-mirror band 6; radiometric interpretation plausible, units require source metadata)
cond_surf (owner-mirror band 17; fold-local rank strata, units unverified)
hypotheses.signature: Find magnetic ridges that persist across 300–1000 m smoothing but lose their co-located surface total-count edge in low-relief, deeper-conductive-base strata. Match sampling within fold-local B17 conductivity-rank strata and train any regime threshold on visible-training cells only. Compare this radiometric-quiet branch with the same magnetic-edge model and sampling without the branch.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A subsurface contrast may remain magnetically visible while young sediment conceals a surface lithologic or scarp expression, a plausible omission regime for surface mapping. Radiometric quietness is a cover/measurement hypothesis, not positive evidence of a geothermal vent or a fault by itself.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: MSPTCD treats terrain-normalized total-count edges as an additional positive feature. This proposal instead tests explicit cross-modal edge disappearance as a cover-conditioned transfer rule, with matched sampling and a negative control. The earlier conductivity-flank and depth-offset ideas are already implemented and are not reused as new hypotheses.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Moist soil, uniform sediment composition, variable aircraft clearance, weak radiometric signal or a buried non-faulted volcanic/plutonic contact can produce the same discordance.

hypotheses.title: Catalogue-free edge-orientation transport through structural junctions
hypotheses.potential_label: Exploratory qualitative potential; high cost and nonunique geological interpretation
layers: det_elev (owner-mirror band 12; detrended, not an absolute hydrologic DEM)
hypotheses.signature: Build an edge graph from label-free gravity and magnetic ridges. Transport axial normals along each ridge across scales, measure tangent continuity and curvature at independently supported intersections, and retain junction branches only when both fields support their geometry. Do not seed the graph with catalogue endpoints.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Blind transfer structures can interrupt or join subsurface property boundaries where no continuous surface fault is mapped. The proposed graph tests independent geophysical geometry rather than completing a known catalogue trace. Geometric complexity alone is not evidence of heat or permeability.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The local implementation has per-pixel Hessian ridges, local cross-field alignment and greedy coverage, but no along-edge orientation-transport graph or cross-field junction consistency. It is not another tip-extension or mapped-stepover prior; global novelty is unverified.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Intersecting dikes, unfaulted intrusive boundaries, erosional drainage intersections and acquisition seams can generate stable junctions.

hypotheses.disconfirmation: Reject if the junction branch fails a same-budget paired holdout comparison or if rotating one field gives comparable gains.

hypotheses.title: Survey-axis notch-stability veto on gridded edge evidence
hypotheses.potential_label: Lowest direct discovery potential; an artefact-control test, not an independent survey
layers: USGS published flight-line geometry metadata, no new line-level binary required for this gridded stress test
hypotheses.signature: In identically tapered local windows of the cached grids, stress-test magnetic/radiometric edges with conservative orientation-selective spectral attenuation around the documented survey-axis directions. Fit allowable attenuation only on visible-training data and compare with rotated-axis controls. Retain only positions whose cross-field edge evidence remains stable, while measuring loss of genuine faults parallel to the axes. Do not impose one global survey-block filter.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Reducing acquisition-line false positives could leave more emission budget for unmapped geological structures. Stability under a notch is only an artefact-sensitivity test; it cannot prove independent repeatability or establish fault presence.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: No survey-axis spectral perturbation stability test is implemented in the local MSPTCD feature set. Unlike the older cross-flight-line proposal, this can be tested using cached grids; true independent flight/tie-line confirmation still needs external observations and is not claimed viable here.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Real east-west or north-south faults may be attenuated; gridding, resampling, dike swarms and anisotropic lithology can also appear directionally stable.
hypotheses.data_status: All named raw bands were restored via the unchanged pinned shared cache builder from the 418,912,844-byte public mirror (SHA-256 4371c82e3b8339b807bdffcf4ef59a225520fe2988d521be208ae33743123bc5). No new external binary is needed for this proposed test. Mirror origin/units are not authenticated as organizer bytes; ignored caches must be verified again before use. No feature or model for this proposal was implemented or evaluated. The USGS release documents east-west flight lines, north-south ties, variable clearance and distinct survey areas; a single global notch would be inappropriate. This proposal is limited to a local-grid sensitivity test; independent flight-line validation still needs unavailable binaries.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Reject if mapped fault orientations parallel to flight directions lose recovery, or if a randomized-axis notch performs as well.
